What is AI Fluency?

AI Fluency means having the knowledge and practical understanding needed to use, evaluate, and communicate effectively about Artificial Intelligence.

It's not just about writing prompts or using ChatGPT.

It's about understanding what AI can do, where it has limitations, how different AI technologies work, and how to apply them responsibly in everyday tasks.Whether you're a college student, software engineer, business owner, or someone completely new to AI, developing AI Fluency can help you become more confident with modern technology.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) Explained

What exactly is Artificial Intelligence?

How is AI different from traditional software?

Why are companies investing in AI-powered products and services?

We'll explore the fundamentals of AI and understand how intelligent systems can support tasks such as content generation, data analysis, automation, decision-making, and problem-solving.

Machine Learning (ML) vs Deep Learning (DL)

You've probably heard the terms Machine Learning and Deep Learning.

But what's the actual difference?

In this video, we'll break down these concepts using simple, real-world examples.

You'll understand how Machine Learning systems learn patterns from data and how Deep Learning uses multi-layer neural networks to solve more complex problems.

What is Generative AI?

ChatGPT, Claude AI, and Google Gemini have made Generative AI accessible to millions of people.

But what makes Generative AI different from traditional AI?

We'll explore how Generative AI systems can create text, images, code, and other content based on user instructions.You'll also understand why Generative AI has become an important technology for developers, content creators, students, and businesses.

What is an LLM (Large Language Model)?

What exactly happens when you ask ChatGPT a question?

What is a Large Language Model?

How do LLMs generate responses?

We'll explain LLM fundamentals, their capabilities, limitations, and why models such as GPT, Claude, and Gemini are important in modern AI applications.

What is RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)?

Can AI answer questions using your own documents and business knowledge?

That's where RAG comes in.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a technique that allows AI applications to retrieve relevant information from external knowledge sources and use it while generating responses.

We'll explore why RAG is useful for document-based chatbots, enterprise knowledge assistants, customer support systems, and other AI applications.

What are AI Agents and Agentic AI?

AI Agents are becoming an important part of modern AI development.

But what makes an AI Agent different from a regular chatbot?

We'll explore how AI Agents can use tools, follow instructions, interact with external systems, and execute multi-step workflows.

You'll also understand the concept of Agentic AI and how it relates to automation and task execution.

What are AI Agent Kits and Frameworks?

You may have heard about Agent Kits, AI frameworks, and AI development tools.

What are they?

Why do developers use them?

We'll discuss how these tools provide components and capabilities that help developers build AI-powered applications and agent workflows.

What are Tokens in AI?

Why do AI models use tokens instead of simply counting words?

Tokens are fundamental units used by language models to process text.Understanding tokens can help you make sense of context windows, API usage, model limitations, and AI application costs.

What is MCP (Model Context Protocol)?

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol.

It is an open protocol that standardizes how AI applications connect with external tools, data sources, and services.MCP helps developers build AI applications that can interact with external systems through a common interface.Instead of creating completely different integrations for every AI application, developers can use MCP-compatible clients and servers to support reusable tool connections.

What Were the Problems with Old MCP?

Earlier MCP implementations could rely on protocol-level sessions and initialization handshakes.For remote deployments, managing sessions across multiple server instances could introduce additional infrastructure complexity.Developers sometimes needed session-aware routing or shared session storage to support horizontally scaled MCP servers.As MCP adoption increased, scalability, reliability, and simpler server infrastructure became increasingly important.

The Biggest MCP Update: Stateless Architecture

One of the most significant changes in the 2026 MCP specification is the move toward a stateless protocol core.The updated architecture removes the previous protocol-level initialization handshake and session requirements.Requests can carry the information needed for processing without relying on an existing protocol session.This makes it easier to deploy MCP servers using conventional HTTP infrastructure and load balancing.

We'll explore what this change means and why it matters for production AI applications.

Old MCP vs New MCP – What's Changed?

In this video, we'll compare important aspects of the earlier and updated MCP specifications.

We'll explore:

• Stateful vs Stateless MCP
• MCP Client and Server Communication
• Initialization Handshake Changes
• Session Management and Scalability
• MCP Tool Discovery
• Multi Round-Trip Requests
• MCP Extensions and Tasks
• Security and Authorization Improvements
• MCP Server Deployment Considerations

Understanding these differences can help developers evaluate how newer MCP capabilities fit into their AI Agent architectures.

.Should You Upgrade Your MCP Server?

If you've already built an MCP server or integrated MCP into an AI Agent, understanding the specification changes is important.However, not every existing MCP integration requires an immediate migration.
Before upgrading, developers should review client compatibility, SDK support, breaking changes, security requirements, and deployment considerations.

This video will help you understand the major differences so you can make informed decisions about your MCP implementations.

Who Should Watch This Video?

This tutorial is useful for:

• AI Agent Developers
• Claude Code Users
• Agentic AI Engineers
• Generative AI Developers
• MCP Server Developers
• AI Automation Enthusiasts
• Students Learning AI Engineering

If you're interested in building AI applications that connect with external tools and services, understanding MCP is an important part of modern AI development.

The Future of MCP & AI Agents

MCP is evolving and AI developers should understand what's changing!

From stateless communication to improved scalability and new extensions, the updated MCP specification introduces important architectural improvements.Watch this complete tutorial to understand the Old MCP vs New MCP, why the changes were introduced, and what they mean for AI Agent development.
